messages:
incident-bot: Pager — HIGH error-rate alert for inference-prod in az1a. 5xx spike ~22% and tail latency > 2s for last 3m. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/incidents/az-egress. Incident ID: INC-20260412-781.

sre_oncall_jaya: ack. I'm on it. assigning severity P1, paging eng-runtime. @eng_runtime_tom can you grab traces + recent kvcache evictions?

eng_runtime_tom: looking. seeing repeated `NETDEV WATCHDOG` and `tx_queue_stop` in kernel.logs on a subset of g5 instances in az1a. past 10m: frequent tx timeouts. snippet:

```
Apr 12 18:22:11 ip-10-0-5-23 kernel: NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (ena): transmit queue 0 timed out
Apr 12 18:22:11 ip-10-0-5-23 kernel: ena 0000:00:03.0: tx timeout, resetting device
Apr 12 18:22:13 ip-10-0-5-23 systemd: Stopping inference-worker.service...
```

eng_infra_sam: same host-level telemetry shows egress queue depth spikes on the host's NICs and host-level soft IRQ backlog rising. I also see higher retransmits to the local resolver in az1a. Not seeing widespread ENI detach, more of a transient TX hang on some hypervisors.

prod_telemetry_bot: Alert: 22% 5xx in route /v1/generate (inference-prod) in az1a, p95 latency 2.8s, p99 6.1s. Error signatures: ECONNRESET, read timeout.

sre_oncall_jaya: immediate mitigations: 1) Drain affected AZ from production traffic lane (soft steer) 2) Kick problematic instances from pool 3) Start packet capture on one repro host and upload to /shared/incidents/INC-20260412-781/pcaps.

eng_runtime_tom: for soft steer, run: 
```
# adjust router weights
prod-router set-weights --cluster inference-prod --weights az1a=0.2,az1b=0.8
```
I'll start draining the most errored nodes (id list from telemetry).

eng_infra_sam: drilling into host console now. if this is kernel tx hang, kernel panic resets are possible if we force reattach. prefer drain+evict approach. I'll attach host-level smoke test for other AZs.

customer_success_elaine: flagged top 5 customers hitting 5xx — outreach in progress. sending initial note: "We're aware of degraded inference in one region (az1a). We're routing traffic to healthy zones; engineering is investigating. We'll update in 30 minutes."

eng_runtime_tom: collected dmesg & `ethtool -S eth0 | egrep '(tx_|rx_)|watchdog'` output and uploaded to incident dir. snippet:
```
ethtool -S eth0
 txq_packets: 123456
 txq_drops: 452
 tx_timeout: 7
```

prod_telemetry_bot: Customer impact summary: 4 accounts impacted with >5% error budget burn, 12% of total requests from az1a degraded. No data plane errors logged for embeddings endpoints.

sre_oncall_jaya: decision: full soft-eviction of az1a traffic (weight 0.15) while we continue diagnostics. notify infra to not reboot hypervisors yet. we want graceful eviction to ensure KV cache doesn't cold-start everywhere.

eng_infra_sam: started targeted instance eviction sequence. command used:
```
infractl evict --hosts h-az1a-[23,45,68] --grace 60s
```
Doing tcpdump on one host: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /shared/incidents/INC-20260412-781/host1.pcap`

eng_runtime_tom: after eviction and weight change p50 latency back to ~180ms for routed traffic; 5xx dropped to 6% in the last 2m. still some residual errors from sticky sessions to evicted nodes.

customer_success_elaine: updating customers with follow-up: "We've steered traffic away from the affected AZ; latency and error rates are improving. Our eng team is continuing root cause analysis and will provide a postmortem."

eng_infra_sam: kernel team requested `dmesg` and `modinfo ena` from one affected host. collecting kernel module versions, and will open a ticket with cloud provider if we see hypervisor-wide driver degradation.

eng_runtime_tom: note: kvcache misses increased when we drained traffic but we used incremental drain to minimize cold starts. started a canary flow to confirm correctness on az1b.

prod_telemetry_bot: Metric update: 5xx now 1.8% cluster-wide, az1a local still ~4.5% but trending down. P99 350ms.

sre_oncall_jaya: action items for now: - keep az1a weight at 0.15 - continue evicting suspicious hosts - collect pcaps + dmesg + kernel module info - CS to send customer update - notify rotations for postmortem (assign eng_runtime_tom, eng_infra_sam)

customer_success_elaine: posted status to affected customers and support channels. pasted message: 
"Status: We observed transient network egress issues in one AZ causing increased errors for inference. Traffic has been rerouted; service performance is recovering. We'll follow up with details and an RCA."

eng_infra_sam: opened provider ticket with trace id 0x7f8a33 — they requested `system logs + ethtool stats` from affected hypervisors. sharing upload link.

eng_runtime_tom: a couple of minutes ago we saw a single host come back to healthy after `ifdown/ifup` on ena. I'm cautious about mass restarting NICs; prefer replacing instance by eviction.

prod_telemetry_bot: Update at 18:34 UTC: cluster 5xx 0.9%, az1a 1.6%.

sre_oncall_jaya: preparing handoff to nightshift: summary for next oncall - current state: degraded but recovering, soft steer in place, evictions ongoing, provider engaged, CS notified. set incident status -> monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260412-781 status changed to MONITORING. Assigned: eng_runtime_tom, eng_infra_sam.

eng_runtime_tom: backing out temporary router change in 10m if metrics remain stable:
```
prod-router set-weights --cluster inference-prod --weights az1a=0.6,az1b=0.4
```
Will coordinate with infra before full weight restore.

customer_success_elaine: preparing a short customer-facing post: "We experienced a partial AZ egress network issue affecting inference in az1a. We rerouted traffic to healthy AZs, and service performance has been restored. We'll publish a detailed RCA once investigations complete."

prod_telemetry_bot: Final update at 18:47 UTC: Cluster 5xx back to baseline 0.3%, az1a 0.5%. No ongoing evictions.

sre_oncall_jaya: marking incident resolved for pager purposes. starting postmortem doc and will attach collected artifacts: pcaps, dmesg, ethtool stats, infractl logs. oncall handoff notes added.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260412-781 — RESOLVED. Closing pager.

eng_infra_sam: create follow-up: open a runbook update to include guidance on incremental eviction vs NIC reload and to add an automated router soft-steer play for similar egress stalls.

eng_runtime_tom: noted for postmortem: evaluate kvcache eviction sensitivity to AZ weight changes; check warmup behavior to reduce customer impact on future drains.

customer_success_elaine: I'll schedule customer-facing RCA next week once we have root cause from infra + provider. thanks team :thumbsup:
